No raw span documenting the pulmonary embolism as chronic or incidental rather than acute
No raw span excluding pulmonary embolism as the cause of the pleuritic chest pain and oxygen desaturation
decisive_items: Computed tomography angiography:  Image Title: Initial CT angiography  Image Description: Shows pulmonary embolism in the right pulmonary artery branching into segmental and lobar arteries, left segmental artery embolus
Oxygen saturation dropped to 70%- Required non-rebreather mask to maintain O2 saturation of 90%
Pleural fluid analysis: Exudate with malignant cells
response.rationale: R4 is the only candidate anchored by a raw CTA span explicitly naming pulmonary embolism with segmental/lobar arterial distribution; this directly explains the acute pleuritic chest pain, severe hypoxemia, and right-heart-strain context. R2 has direct cytologic confirmation of a malignant effusion, but it is a coexisting complication rather than the acute culprit; R1 merely restates known cancer history, and R3 describes a physiologic consequence without a distinct etiologic diagnosis.

rejected.why: The raw support spans only recite the known ovarian serous carcinoma history and do not establish recurrent carcinoma as the cause of the acute ED presentation.
The raw span documents hypoxemia and oxygen dependence, which is a consequence/complication of PE or effusion, not an etiologic diagnosis with specific anatomy.
